summary: Obfuscated payload in Socket-layer module of Baileys fork executes on import
details: @nexustechpro/baileys is a rename/fork of the widely-used @whiskeysockets/baileys WhatsApp library. Every JavaScript file in the package is plain source EXCEPT lib/Socket/chats.js, which is fully obfuscated with obfuscator.io — hex-escaped import specifiers, rotated string array, and a self-invoking decoder IIFE at file top. lib/Socket/chats.js is re-exported through lib/Socket/index.js and lib/index.js (the package `main`), so the obfuscated IIFE runs at the moment a consumer `require()`s or `import`s the package. The surrounding fork is otherwise a clone of the upstream library, so the obfuscation is not explained by any legitimate build step — plain source everywhere else, opaque bytes exactly in the Socket layer that handles chats, message send/receive, and session/credential material. The concrete network destinations, credential reads, and any exec sinks are hidden behind the decoder and cannot be enumerated from the shipped bytes, but the shape — a name-scope fork of a WhatsApp session library with one selectively-obfuscated Socket module wired into `main` — matches the WhatsApp session/credential theft pattern seen in prior Baileys fork compromises.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
